layout_structure.title_text: SLAM3R: Real-Time Dense Scene Reconstruction from Monocular RGB Videos
layout_structure.layout_description: This is a title slide with a centered layout on a plain white background. At the top right, there is a logo for the CVPR Nashville conference. The main title is centered and uses multiple colors: 'SLAM3R' in red, 'Real-Time' in blue, and 'Dense Scene Reconstruction' in green. Below this, a subtitle 'from Monocular RGB Videos' is centered, with the last three words in orange. Underneath the title, the authors' names are listed in two rows, followed by their numbered affiliations in a third row. At the bottom of the slide, four institutional logos (Peking University, The University of Hong Kong, Aalto University, and VIVO) are arranged in a horizontal row, corresponding to the affiliations listed above. The text density is light, and the overall design is clean and professional.

The slide features a large, left-aligned title at the top in a serif font. Below the title, the content is organized into two distinct columns. The left column contains a large grayscale image showing a 3D cloud-like reconstruction, with the caption '3D assets creation' centered below it. The right column contains a complex grid of images representing 'Robotic mapping and navigation'. This grid consists of two larger images at the top (a top-down view of a room with robots and a 2D occupancy map) followed by two rows of six smaller thumbnails each, displaying color-coded depth maps and their corresponding RGB camera views. A single-line citation is located at the very bottom-left of the slide. The overall design is clean with a white background and light text density, prioritizing visual demonstrations over text.

The slide follows a clean, two-column layout with a large serif-font title positioned at the top left. Below the title, two distinct visual examples are presented side-by-side. The left column features a single large image of a 3D reconstructed outdoor scene with buildings and trees, captioned '3D assets creation' directly below it. The right column contains a composite image illustrating 'Robotic mapping and navigation'. This composite includes a main view of a robot in a room, a 2D top-down map with colored trajectory lines, and a grid of smaller thumbnails showing depth maps and camera views. At the very bottom left, there is a small line of text citing the source: 'Multi-robot collaborative dense scene reconstruction. SIGGRAPH 2019.' The background is plain white, and the overall text density is light, focusing primarily on visual demonstrations.

layout_structure.layout_type: single column with title and figure
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide uses a clean white background with a large, serif-font title 'Problem definition' aligned to the top-left. Below the title, a single line of text states the primary goal: 'Reconstruct dense 3D point cloud of a scene from RGB videos'. This is followed by two bullet points that define the 'Input' (RGB video with unknown camera parameters) and 'Output' (dense 3D points in a unified coordinate system), with key terms highlighted in bold. The bottom section of the slide features a visual flow diagram: on the left is a sample frame from an indoor RGB video, followed by a bright blue horizontal arrow pointing to the right, which leads to a visualization of a dense 3D point cloud of the same scene. Each image has a centered label underneath it ('RGB video' and 'Dense 3D points'). The text density is light, prioritizing a clear visual representation of the problem statement.

The slide follows a clean, single-column layout on a plain white background. The title 'Motivation' is placed at the top-left in a large, black serif font. The main body of the slide consists of a hierarchical bulleted list with three levels of indentation. The first level introduces 'Previous works on dense reconstruction'. The second level details classical and recent deep learning methods, with the third level specifically critiquing 'DROID-SLAM' and 'NICER-SLAM'. Key phrases such as 'complex systems', 'time consuming', 'low reconstruction quality', and 'slow running time' are highlighted in bold for emphasis. Below the bulleted list, a summary statement 'Our goal: real-time and high-quality reconstruction' is positioned, with the latter part in bold to emphasize the project's objective. At the bottom-left corner, four lines of academic references are provided in a significantly smaller font size. The overall text density is light, making the slide easy to read.

The slide has a minimalist design with a plain white background and black text. The title 'Motivation' is located at the top-left in a large, serif font. The main body of the slide consists of a hierarchical bulleted list that outlines the limitations of previous work. The first level of the list introduces 'Previous works on dense reconstruction'. Below this, two sub-bullets categorize these works into classical systems and recent deep learning methods, with key drawbacks like 'complex systems', 'time consuming', 'low reconstruction quality', and 'slow running time' highlighted in bold. layout_structure.layout_type: single column with title and diagram
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide has a clean, white background with a large, serif-font title 'Motivation' at the top-left. Below it, a sub-heading 'Review of DUSt3R' introduces two bullet points that summarize the features and a key limitation of the method. The bottom two-thirds of the slide are occupied by a detailed technical diagram illustrating the DUSt3R architecture. This diagram shows a dual-branch pipeline where two input images of a cube are processed through 'Patchify' modules, 'ViT encoders' with shared weights, 'Transformer Decoders' with information sharing, and prediction 'Heads'. The output of these heads consists of 'Pointmaps' and 'Confidence' maps, which are then visualized on the right as 3D point clouds within a common coordinate frame, including camera frustums. Mathematical notation for tensor dimensions (e.g., R^WxHx3) is used throughout the diagram. A small citation for the CVPR 2024 paper is located at the very bottom-left corner.

layout_structure.layout_type: single column with title and horizontal sections
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a large, left-aligned title at the top in a black serif font. The content is organized into two distinct horizontal sections, each corresponding to a specific module of the proposed system. Each section begins with a bold bullet point followed by a brief text description. Below the text, there is a visual representation consisting of a flowchart on the left and qualitative results on the right, separated by a vertical dashed line. The first section for the 'Image-to-Points module' shows a sequence of images entering an 'I2P' red box to generate local pointmaps, with three 3D point cloud visualizations to the right. The second section for the 'Local-to-World module' shows scene and local data entering an 'L2W' green box to produce an updated scene, with three 3D visualizations on the right showing the incremental building of a room model. The diagrams use colored rectangular boxes (red, green, blue, orange) and black arrows to denote data flow. The overall text density is moderate, set against a clean white background.

The slide uses a horizontal comparison layout to contrast two neural network architectures. A large, centered title is positioned at the top. The main body is divided into two rows: the top row is labeled 'DUSt3R' and the bottom row is labeled 'Image-to-Points'. Each row contains a detailed architectural flowchart. On the left of each flowchart are input images (a single keyframe and one or more supporting frames). These lead into a 'Shared ViT encoder' block. Following the encoder, the data flows through 'Decoder block 0' (containing red 'D_key' and blue 'D_sup' components), then through eleven additional 'Decoder blocks'. On the right side, 'Head' modules produce final outputs, which are labeled with mathematical notation for points (P) and confidence (C) and accompanied by colorful point-cloud visualizations. The 'Image-to-Points' section specifically highlights the extension to multiple supporting frames (L-1) through stacked input images and duplicated decoder/head components. The background is plain white, and the text density is moderate, focusing on component labels and output variables.

The slide features a large, centered title at the top. The main content is organized into two horizontal layers: a faded-out top layer representing the original 'DUSt3R' architecture and a prominent bottom layer labeled 'Image-to-Points' representing the proposed method. On the left, a stack of input images (one key frame and multiple supporting frames) feeds into a 'Shared ViT encoder' block. The resulting features pass through a series of decoder blocks, starting with 'Decoder block 0'. A red dashed line connects the 'D_key' component of this block to a large, red-bordered callout box on the top right, which provides a detailed schematic of the internal layers: Self-attention, Multi-view cross-attention, and Feed-forward. Within this callout, a sub-diagram further details the cross-attention and max-pooling mechanism. The main pipeline continues through eleven more decoder blocks to two output heads, which produce point maps and confidence maps visualized as colorful images on the far right. The diagram uses a clean color scheme with blue and red accents for key components and black arrows to indicate data flow.

layout_structure.title_text: Local-to-World: I2P augmented with pointmap embedding
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a large, centered title at the top in a black serif font. The main body of the slide is occupied by a complex architectural flow diagram that moves generally from left to right. On the far left, input images are shown in two groups: a stack labeled 'Sce. i ... Sce. k' and a single 'Key.' image below it. These feed into a yellow rectangular block describing visual feature retrieval. Above the central area, several colorful pointmaps feed into an encoder block labeled 'E_pts'. The core of the diagram consists of 'Decoder block 0', which contains an orange 'D_sce' block and a green 'D_reg' block, followed by a large vertical rectangle representing eleven additional decoder blocks. On the right side, the flow splits into two prediction heads ('Head1' and 'Head2'). 'Head1' produces 'Refined points' and confidence scores, illustrated by a stack of output pointmaps. 'Head2' produces 'New registered points' and a confidence score, illustrated by a single output pointmap. The diagram uses various colored blocks (yellow, orange, green), arrows to indicate data flow, and mathematical notation for variables. The background is plain white, and the text density is moderate, consisting primarily of technical labels.

layout_structure.title_text: Retrieval module: Lightweight extension of I2P
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a large, centered architectural diagram on a plain white background, topped by a serif-font title. The diagram illustrates a data flow from left to right: it begins with a stack of input images (Key and Support images) entering a 'Shared ViT encoder'. The resulting features pass through two sets of 'Decoder blocks' (x2 and x10). Several components are marked with snowflake icons, indicating they are frozen. A specific 'Retrieval head' is highlighted in yellow with a fire icon, signifying it is the trainable part of the module. This head outputs correlation scores that feed into an 'MSE loss' block at the bottom right. On the far right, the final outputs are shown as both text labels (Points and Confidence scores) and corresponding colorful heatmap images. A concluding caption at the bottom center states that the retrieval module is trained from the I2P module.
